animations._comment: Opening animation modes. 'id' becomes the `data-animation` attribute of <html>/<body> and therefore selects the flavour declared in css/animations/; 'labelKey' is the translation of the picker button; 'parodic' flags a mode that is deliberately ridiculous (the settings screen advertises it); 'tearMs'/'flipMs'/'staggerMs' are the durations in milliseconds (opening of the pack, one card flip, delay between two summary cards) applied through the `--anim-tear-ms`/`--anim-flip-ms`/`--anim-stagger-ms` custom properties, so a mode only needs numbers here. 'normal' is the cinematic base (see css/components/card-reveal.css and css/views/opening.css), 'epic' stages it (light rays, shockwave, motes) and 'explosive' is the joke one (confetti, stickers, shake). A mode declared without a matching CSS block simply reuses the base animation at its own speed. The Mine Pick reads the very same durations.

foil._comment: Strength of the foil of the super rare, legendary and mythic printings, as a percentage of the intensity it was designed at. The four values bound the first slider of the settings screen; 'min' at 0 switches the foil off completely (the planes become transparent and their animation is stopped), and 'default' is what a new account starts at and what a player who never opens the slider keeps seeing. js/utils/FoilManager.js publishes the value as `--foil-intensity` (a 0-1 factor) on <html>, which css/components/card-shine.css multiplies into the opacity of its planes. A value outside the range is CLAMPED, never rejected: narrowing the range later must stay safe for saves written with a wider one.

glare._comment: Strength of the SECOND slider of the foil panel ('Brillance'): the bright line that sweeps across the artwork, back and forth, on top of the foil's shapes. It has its own range and its own preference because the two effects are independent - a player can keep the honeycomb and the embossing while muting the moving line, or the other way round. FoilManager publishes it as `--glare-intensity` (a 0-1 factor) on <html>; the line is drawn by the `.card-shine__gleam` layer. Same clamping rule as the foil above.

boosters._comment: 'extraBoosterPriceSparks' is the price of ONE extra daily booster, bought with Sparks once the free daily boosters ('dailyFreeBoosters') are all spent. A bought booster is kept in the quota under its own bucket, is spent AFTER the daily quota and the redeem/gift bonuses of an extension (so a free booster is never wasted by a purchase), and - unlike the daily allowance - is NOT cleared by the daily reset: it was paid for.

minePick._comment: Mine Pick. The daily board holds 'boosterCount' SIMULATED openings, built from the real booster parameters: 'boosters.cardsPerBooster', the rarity table of each extension (which may override 'defaultRarity.json') and 'boosters.godpackChancePercent'. A simulated pack is therefore drawn exactly like an opened one. 'picksPerDay' free picks per UTC day (reset at midnight UTC, like the daily boosters), 'historySize' picks kept for the statistics. The board is deterministic: it is seeded with 'seedSalt' + the UTC day + the account UUID, so a reload shows the same board, it changes at the next UTC day, and two accounts never share one (changing 'seedSalt' rebuilds the board of the CURRENT day, and the boosters already picked become stale). The extension of each booster is drawn at random with a weight of (rank + 1) ** 'setWeightExponent': the extension whose id ranks highest is the most likely.

mining._comment: Mine (MineBlock). The rules of the blocks themselves - the five kinds, their 'Weight' (the chance of falling on one), their 'Hardness' (the number of taps needed to break one) and their loot (a guaranteed 'dust', sometimes 'Sparks') - live in 'configPath', so the mine can be rebalanced without touching this file. 'blocksPerDay' blocks are offered every UTC day (reset at midnight UTC, like the daily boosters and the Mine Pick) and they are mined ONE BY ONE: the next block is only drawn once the previous one is broken. The order of the day is seeded with 'seedSalt' + the UTC day + the account UUID, so a reload resumes the very block that was being mined and two accounts never share the same sequence. 'nextBlockDelayMs' is how long the broken block stays on screen before the next one drops in (the rewards keep flying while it does): a small value keeps the mining fast, a large one lets the loot be admired.

promos._comment: Promo cards. 'directory' holds one file per series ('A1.json' -> the 'A1-Promo' group), an entry being a card built exactly like a booster card ('Index', 'Name_XX', 'Desc_XX', 'Rarity', 'Style', 'Layout', 'Path'). Promo cards are NEVER drawn from a booster: they only enter the collection through a redeem code or a gift, only appear in the collection when they are owned, and never count in a completion ratio. 'sets' lists the files to load; leave it empty to load one file per booster extension of 'boosters.sets'. A series without a promo file simply has no promo.

timeSync.comment: Providers are tried in order. 'format' tells DateSyncManager how to read the payload: json (object), trace (key=value lines), headers (HTTP response headers). Order is driven by browser reachability: a provider without Access-Control-Allow-Origin cannot be read from a page. See js/business/DateSyncManager.js.

sparks._comment: Sparks currency. 'sellPrice'/'buyPrice' map a rarity (1-5) to its value in Sparks; 'boosterReward' is credited on every booster opening. Every key falls back to its built-in default when absent.

useritemCode._comment: Step 10 personal codes. 'key' is 32 random bytes in base64 ('openssl rand -base64 32'); the value below is a PLACEHOLDER (32 zero bytes) that MUST be replaced, with the same value in the game master generator. WARNING: this key is served to the browser, so anyone reading the sources can forge codes (see .docs/gamemaster/useritemcode.md section 2).

levelling._comment: the default level is 'defaultLevel'. To level up the first level, you need 'baseRequiredExpToLevelUp' XP, and each level, the requirement increase by 'incrementRequiredXpBy' XP. 'experience' is the XP earned from the account itself: every booster opened, every distinct card of the collection, and a custom player name (not 'profile.defaultName').

ExperiencePerTrophy._comment: Trophies gives thoses experience with thoses rarity. Except if it's explicitly said in the trophy json

trophies._comment: Trophy catalogue. 'boostersConfigPath' holds the tiers recurring on every extension (completion + opened boosters), 'globalConfigPath' the account wide tiers, and 'directory' one file per extension (<setId>.json) listing the collection trophies. The XP of a trophy comes from 'ExperiencePerTrophy', unless its JSON declares its own 'Experience'.

profile._comment: Player profile. 'maxFavorites' is the number of cards pinnable in the collection, 'maxFeaturedTrophies' the number of unlocked trophies highlighted on the profile page, and 'defaultName' the name that does NOT grant the 'nameChanged' experience (empty = any typed name counts).

profileIcons._comment: Profile avatars. 'defaultPath' lists the icons every account can select from the start, 'unlockablePath' the icons that a trophy unlocks (matched by name), and 'directory' holds one <setId>.json per extension mapping a collection trophy name to the icons it unlocks.
